scope: E01 BurnNand preflight through the first program-call boundary, one anonymous program/readback helper, and the installed-header user-area predicate. Offline original-MIPS replay with modeled storage.

findings.entry: BurnNand 0x80012654 reaches the original BurnGetSectionsMap 0x8001a710 from 0x80012fe8 before modeled storage. The card callback is supplied exactly 131072 original package bytes at [0x1000c0,0x1200c0). Header selectors 0 and 1 both receive the synthetic installed header; geometry is one synthetic zone, 1024 blocks, 256 sectors/block, 512 bytes/sector.
findings.preflight: Native code requests three op-6 calls and one op-8 call per synthetic block 0..639, then two op-6 calls per block 640..1023, and three additional op-6 calls at sectors 0,1,0 before the first op-5 request. Op 6 uses sector locations, op 8 uses block locations. The original code runs the loop and dispatches those requests; the harness models their results.
findings.user_area: The installed-header fixture uses +0x310=640, +0x314=384, +0x234 byte=1. The separate handle byte +0x1268 is 1. BlockUserArea 0x800117d0 requires a nonzero +0x314 count and +0x234 byte, then checks unsigned inclusive range [start, start+count-1]. Seven replay cases cover both boundaries and the mode/count gates. Op 8 does not reach 640..1023 in this synthetic preflight; the firmware still issues op-6 reads for that range.
findings.program_boundary: The first op-5 request stops at FcuNandOperation 0x8008249c with link 0x80011e10; it has sector 0, count 256, primary pointer 0x10010000 and 16-byte extra buffer. BurnNand call 0x80013aa8 supplies extra at its stack +0x128, matching the captured argument address. The prefix does not execute op 5. The report separately hashes the card chunk and native program source at that boundary, where 281 bytes differ.
findings.program_helper: Anonymous 0x80011da8 computes sector=block*handle[0x1238], count=handle[0x1238] and sends op 5 with caller's data and extra. On status 0 it sends op 4 with handle[0x1250] as readback buffer and zero extra fields. On two successful statuses it compares exactly count*512 bytes until the first mismatch. A nonzero status or mismatch returns 0 and stores byte 0x78 at map[block] when a map is provided. Equality returns 1.

storage_dispatch.boundary: All FCU calls are intercepted in replay. The following dispatch addresses and command choices are static original-code evidence.
storage_dispatch.wrapper: FcuNandOperation 0x8008249c passes through to FcuNandOperationEx 0x80081808 by default. For op 4 with global byte 0x800b785b==1, it tail-calls FcuSsfdcOperationEx 0x80080de0.
storage_dispatch.jump_table: FcuNandOperationEx indexes 0x800a4e24 by operation minus 4 at 0x80081be4..0x80081c04.

storage_dispatch.downstream: Configured branches converge at 0x80081dbc to FcuOperation 0x8007ee30. The role labels describe firmware request construction; the physical flash protocol, erase behavior, and controller timing were not replayed.

trace_limitations: Typed function extents are from original E01 ELF32 STT_FUNC size and match both PT_LOAD and section offsets.
Anonymous code extents are analyst-bounded from original instructions. They do not have a typed ELF size.
Transfer lists are linear scans. Reachability is only asserted in the bounded replay.

evidence.role: Burn entry, map, block assessment, erase and program call sites
Program followed by readback and byte comparison

reproduction: tools/check_burn_storage.py exposes validate_report(document['replay']) for standard-library metadata checks.
limits: An actual installed-media header and physical bad-block/erase state were not supplied. Geometry, spare bytes, FCU statuses and the standalone readback are modeled.
The real package supplies only the first chunk to the modeled input callback. The separate card short-read/hash analysis is in analysis/loader-foundation.json.

The preflight stops before the first op 5. The helper cases use synthetic one- and two-sector requests. They do not exercise the first real-size 256-sector request past dispatch, all loader chunks, update commit, or persistent storage.
The code-level user-range check and absence of op 8 in this fixture are not device protection guarantees.

notes: K-3 III update validation uses project/type/magic and word sums in a different format; the Q7 E01 map/protection rules are not transferred to it.
Both projects distinguish capability input, command admission and completion. The K-3 III AF command/dispatch evidence does not establish Q7 group2/op4 wire semantics or actuator compatibility.
